title: Tata Steel Greenlights ₹33,873 Crore NINL Expansion to Double Long Products Capacity
excerpt: The board approved a 4.8 MTPA expansion at Neelachal Ispat Nigam in Odisha alongside strong Q1 results, with net profit rising 19% to ₹2,385 crore.
body:
• Tata Steel's board approved ₹33,873 crore (~$4 billion) to add 4.8 million tonnes per annum of long steel capacity at NINL in Odisha, its largest single expansion commitment in India.
  • Q1 FY27 net profit rose 19% to ₹2,385 crore on revenue of ₹60,794 crore, with EBITDA per tonne climbing 23% to ₹12,898.
  • The expansion — featuring rebar mills, a rebar coil mill, and a wire rod mill — could push Tata Steel's total long-product capacity past 10 MTPA, targeting India's construction and infrastructure boom.
  • NINL is being formally merged into Tata Steel after the board approved the amalgamation in March 2026, simplifying the group's corporate structure.

Tata Steel has approved a ₹33,873 crore investment to expand long steel capacity by 4.8 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) at Neelachal Ispat Nigam Ltd (NINL) in Odisha. The decision, announced alongside the company's June-quarter earnings on July 30, converts what had been an in-principle approval into a fully budgeted capital commitment — making it the steelmaker's largest single expansion project in India.

Q1 Numbers Back the Bet

The investment comes from a position of financial strength. Tata Steel posted Q1 FY27 net profit of ₹2,385 crore, up 19% from ₹2,007 crore a year ago. Revenue climbed 14% to ₹60,794 crore, while EBITDA jumped 25% to ₹9,370 crore. EBITDA per tonne — a closely watched metric in the steel sector — improved 23% to ₹12,898.

Sales volume edged up 2% to 7.27 million tonnes. On a standalone India basis, the numbers were sharper: revenue hit ₹36,989 crore and EBITDA reached ₹9,409 crore, with per-tonne EBITDA at ₹18,198.

CEO and Managing Director T.V. Narendran noted that the global operating environment remained complex, with West Asia disruptions hitting supply chains and input costs. But the India business delivered enough cushion for the board to sign off on the expansion.

What the Expansion Looks Like

The NINL plant sits in the Kalinganagar industrial complex in Jajpur district, close to Tata Steel's existing greenfield facility. The 4.8 MTPA expansion is oriented entirely toward long products — two rebar mills of roughly 1 MTPA each, a 0.5 MTPA rebar coil mill, and a high-end wire rod mill, according to earlier disclosures by the company.

Tata Steel currently runs about 5.4 MTPA of long-product capacity across its plants. The NINL build-out would push that past 10 MTPA, a transformative jump that positions the company to capture a larger share of India's infrastructure and construction steel demand. The company plans to supply NINL entirely from its captive Koira iron ore mines, which are being expanded in parallel.

The strategic logic is clear: long products — rebars, structural steel, wire rods — are where volume growth is happening in India. Government-led infrastructure spending and a housing construction cycle have driven steady demand increases. Tata Steel's branded retail network, Tata Tiscon, already serves 10,000 to 12,000 dealers and gives the company a distribution edge that commodity-grade competitors lack.

Execution will take three to four years, placing commissioning around 2029-2030. The Odisha state government had already approved NINL's expansion from its current 0.98 MTPA rated capacity to 9.5 MTPA back in late 2024, clearing a key regulatory hurdle.

Simplifying the Structure

The NINL expansion is happening in tandem with a corporate cleanup. In March 2026, the board approved merging NINL — which Tata Steel acquired through the government's privatization programme in July 2022 for ₹12,100 crore — directly into the parent company. NINL's shares will be cancelled with no new shares issued, keeping the ownership structure unchanged.

The merger is expected to reduce administrative and logistics costs, pool iron ore procurement, and consolidate sales planning. In FY25, NINL posted revenue of ₹5,701 crore and EBITDA of about ₹1,000 crore — a turnaround from the loss-making unit Tata Steel inherited.

The Broader Capital Picture

Tata Steel spent ₹3,579 crore on capex in Q1 alone. Its 0.75 MTPA electric arc furnace plant at Ludhiana is ramping up, and construction continues on a 0.7 MTPA hot-rolled pickling and galvanising line. Gross debt stood at ₹97,985 crore, but liquidity remained robust at ₹45,950 crore including ₹13,221 crore in cash.

The company's European operations showed improvement too. Tata Steel Netherlands received local environmental clearance for trial runs ahead of a full restart. The UK unit at Port Talbot narrowed its EBITDA loss from £48 million in Q4 to £27 million in Q1.

What to Watch

The NINL expansion is now the single biggest swing factor in Tata Steel's India growth story. Analysts have pointed out that the company's ambition to reach 40 MTPA of total capacity by 2030 hinges on timely execution at Kalinganagar, NINL, and Meramandali. With the capex number now locked at ₹33,873 crore, the market will track quarterly spending run-rates and construction milestones closely. Environmental clearances, while expected, remain a gating factor. For investors watching India's steel sector, this is a bet on the country's infrastructure cycle having years left to run.
nri_angle: The expansion positions Tata Steel as a stronger play for NRI investors eyeing India's infrastructure-led growth cycle, while the improving financials and domestic capacity build reduce the group's dependence on volatile European operations.
author: Diaspora Desk
